'''InMoment '''is an American [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] software company headquartered in [[Salt Lake City]], Utah. The company was originally founded as Mindshare Technologies by John Sperry, and Kurt Williams, and Richard D. Hanks in 2002. The current chair and chief executive officer (CEO) is John Lewis. The company provides businesses with insights on customers and employees from information such as comments, surveys, and review data and provides cloud-based software to collect and analyze data from voice, text, and video.

==History==
===Mindshare Technologies===
John Sperry, and Kurt Williams, and Richard D. Hanks co-founded Mindshare Technologies with an initial investment of $40,000 in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 19, 2013 |first=Tom |last=Harvey |title=Survey says: Mindshare buys firm from Canada |url=https://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=56893493&itype=CMSID |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=The Salt Lake Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Daily Research News Online no. 17485 – Marriott Veteran to Chair Mindshare Technologies |url=https://www.mrweb.com/drno/news17485.htm |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=www.mrweb.com}}</ref> The company provided customer insights and surveys for [[Fast-food restaurant|Quick-Serve Restaurant]] (QSR) Chains.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Dishman |first=Lydia |date=October 3, 2011 |title=Mindshare Technologies CEO John Sperry Addresses Your Complaints |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/1784097/mindshare-technologies-ceo-john-sperry-addresses-your-complaints |website=Fast Company}}</ref> By 2011, the company had 85 employees and $18&nbsp;million in annual revenue.<ref name=":0" /> In 2013, the company acquired Empathica, a social customer experience and social media technology company, doubling the size of the company. After the acquisition, Mindshare Technologies was renamed InMoment.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-07-01 |title=After Successfully Rebranding Omniture and Vivint, Kristi Knight Hopes to Do the Same For InMoment |url=https://newsroom.siliconslopes.com/after-successfully-rebranding-omniture-and-vivint-kristi-knight-hopes-to-do-the-same-for-inmoment/ |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=Silicon Slopes Newsroom |language=en}}</ref>

===InMoment===
In 2017, Andrew Joiner was appointed CEO.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |date=2018-05-21 |title=US software company InMoment acquires local consulting firm brandXP |url=https://www.afr.com/technology/us-software-company-inmoment-acquires-local-consulting-firm-brandxp-20180516-h1048c |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=Australian Financial Review |language=en}}</ref> Founding CEO John Sperry remained chief scientist and chairman of InMoment's board of directors. In 2018, the company acquired BrandXP, a customer experience consulting firm, expanding offices into New Zealand and Australia.<ref name="auto"/>

In 2020, [[MaritzCX]] merged with InMoment, retaining the InMoment brand. The deal was backed by private equity firm [[Madison Dearborn Partners]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Madison Dearborn Partners Acquires InMoment {{!}} Mergr M&A Deal Summary |url=https://mergr.com/madison-dearborn-partners-acquires-inmoment |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=mergr.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=InMoment acquires MaritzCX, sets up Battle Royale in EFM industry {{!}} CustomerThink |url=https://customerthink.com/inmoment-acquires-maritzcx-sets-up-battle-royale-in-efm-industry/ |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=customerthink.com |date=3 March 2020 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2021, the company acquired Wootric, an AI-powered platform to measure and boost customer satisfaction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=InMoment Acquires Digital Feedback Solutions Provider Wootric |url=https://www.destinationcrm.com/Articles/CRM-News/CRM-Across-the-Wire/InMoment-Acquires-Digital-Feedback-Solutions-Provider-Wootric-144611.aspx |access-date=2023-05-18 |website=www.destinationcrm.com|date=6 January 2021 }}</ref> In the same year, InMoment acquired [[Lexalytics]], a language processing and analytics company.<ref>{{Cite web  |date=2021-09-09 |title=InMoment completes acquisition of Lexalytics |url=https://www.utahbusiness.com/inmoment-acquires-lexalytics/ |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=Utah Business |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2022, InMoment acquired ReviewTrackers, a customer review and reputation management software company.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Natasha |last=Bach |date=2022-07-06 |title=InMoment acquires ReviewTrackers |url=https://www.prweek.com/article/1792171 |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=www.prweek.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Radlovački |first=Sandra |date=2022-06-17 |title=InMoment Acquires ReviewTrackers |url=https://www.cxtoday.com/voice-of-the-customer/inmoment-acquires-reviewtrackers/ |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=CX Today |language=en-GB}}</ref> In the same year, InMoment's platform became [[Web Content Accessibility Guidelines|WCAG 2.0]] Compliant.<ref>{{Cite web |title=InMoment Updates XI Platform |url=https://www.destinationcrm.com/Articles/CRM-News/CRM-Across-the-Wire/InMoment-Updates-XI-Platform-153717.aspx |date=June 28, 2022 |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=www.destinationcrm.com}}</ref>

==Product==
The InMoment Experience Improvement (XI) Platform is a cloud-based software that collects structured and [[unstructured data]]. The platform uses artificial intelligence and text analytic software to process data into insights for improving customer experience, product experience, and employee retention.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-29 |title=Market Share: Customer Experience and Relationship Management, Worldwide, 2020 |url=https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/4001096 |access-date=2023-02-27 |website=Gartner |language=en}}</ref>
